  I. Background
     In conjunction with DOT's Open Restaurants Program for sidewalk and roadway dining, the Department
     of Buildings shares the following guidance for the types of minor changes owners can make for the safe
     continuation of outdoor dining in restaurants and bars without having to obtain a construction permit
     from the Department of Buildings.


  II. Outdoor Seating in Front of a Restaurant or Bar
     For restaurants and bars seeking permission to place outdoor seating in front of their establishment on
     the sidewalk and/or in the roadway, please apply through NYC Open Restaurant Program, comply with
     the requirements outlined in the guidelines and the conditions listed under the Applications for DOB
     Permit Not Required section below.


  III. Minor Modifications on Private Property NOT Requiring a DOB Permit
     Where an establishment wishes to place outdoor seating on private property and complies with the
     conditions listed under the Applications for DOB Permit Not Required section below, there is no need
     to file with the Department of Buildings for the specified minor modifications.


  IV. Changes Affecting Code Compliance
     The Department encourages restaurants and bars to limit minor modifications within the conditions listed
     under the Applications for DOB Permit Not Required section below so that there is no need to file
     with the Department.
     Where modifications meet the conditions listed under the Applications for DOB Permit Required
     section below, applications for permits from the Department of Buildings are required. Additional
     information on obtaining a permit is available at www1.nyc.gov/site/buildings/business/how-to-
     obtain-a-permit.page. Alternatively, the Department offers a Professional Certification Program
     which enables Professional Engineers (PE) and Registered Architects (RA) to certify that the plans they
     file with the Department comply with all applicable laws. This reduces the amount of time a builder

     V. Maintaining Social Distancing, Building Safety and Accessibility
        Ensure compliance with social distancing required by the State’s Interim Guidance For Outdoor and
        Take-Out/Delivery Food Services During The Covid-19 Public Health Emergency guidance. In any
        case, do not provide less than 15 SF per person when tables and seating are provided in yards*, roofs
        and parking lots.
        *NOTE: Where the only exit from a yard passes through an interior space, the number of occupants in the yard
        must not exceed 74 persons. Roofs without occupancy listed on Certificate of Occupancy or Place of Assembly
        Certificate of Occupancy (PACO) must apply to DOB.

        All other Building Code safety requirements remain in effect and must be observed. Accessible routes
        and features must also be maintained in buildings and outdoor spaces as part of reopening.


     VI. Posting of Dining Capacity
        Where indoor dining is also provided in accordance with NYS Guidance, restaurants must publicly post
        their indoor dining capacity and the phone number and text number at which diners can report violations
        in a conspicuous location at the front entrance. The posting must indicate numbers for both indoor and
        outdoor seating areas.

   VII. Heating for Outdoor Dining
         Refer to Buildings Bulletins for more information on electric (BB 2020-018) and natural gas-fired
         heaters (BB 2020-019). Electric heaters are allowed on both sidewalks and roadways. Propane and
         natural gas heaters are allowed on sidewalks only and are prohibited in roadways. Open flame natural
         gas-fired heaters are not permitted. The use of propane for heating requires a permit from FDNY and
         compliance with FDNY regulations for outdoor use, handling and secure outdoor tank storage
         overnight.
